A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UnZipLoRA. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching material that was reorganized.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation experiments, human preferences, alignment scores, qualitative ablations, and computational measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds quantitative ablations, sensitivity tests, recontextualization preferences, and additional application results.

M1.justification: The three separation mechanisms, losses, SDXL block assignments, and direct-addition inference are retained. V2 expresses the existing column fraction as N, retaining 30% for the main experiments. The additional applications do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds cross-image composition, combining subject and style LoRAs learned from different images (Figures 6 and 19), extending v1's evaluation of decomposition and recombination from one image. Appendix B.4 also adds human-subject evaluations. Both versions still describe a 40-image collection.

E2.justification: The decomposition comparators remain DreamBooth-LoRA, Inspiration Tree, and B-LoRA. V2 expands recontextualization comparisons beyond v1's B-LoRA comparison by reporting preferences against all three methods. Figure 8 also adds B-LoRA outputs to the existing failure cases.

E3.justification: V2 adds component-wise user comparisons, controlled trigger-phrase tests, 20/30/40% column-selection experiments, and KOALA evaluations. The original SDXL budgets and eight-input, sixteen-sample alignment protocol remain. DreamBooth's stated style-training prompt changes from 'A subject in <s> style' to 'A <c> in <s> style'; this reporting revision does not establish rerunning existing comparisons.

E4.justification: V1 primarily supports component contributions through qualitative ablations. V2 adds component preference and alignment tables (Tables 3–4), subject/style trigger-phrase sensitivity tests (Figures 10–11), and column-fraction sensitivity tests (Figure 18). Existing failure analysis also gains a B-LoRA comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. The existing generation-sample protocol and seed-selection discussion are retained; the added user-study sample counts describe new evaluations rather than a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2's alignment scores and Table 1's decomposition preferences remain identical. V2 adds recontextualization preferences of 98.10%, 79.17%, and 77.14% over DreamBooth-LoRA, Inspiration Tree, and B-LoRA, respectively, plus component results in Tables 3–4. Cross-image, KOALA, and sensitivity experiments substantially expand the reported findings.

T1.justification: The low-rank formulation and Equations 1–5 are mathematically unchanged. V2 adds no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation; introducing N names an experimental hyperparameter.

C1.justification: The central claims about single-image decomposition and compatible subject/style LoRAs remain. V2's introduction additionally claims cross-image composition and generalization to KOALA, extending applicability without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explains when generic versus detailed trigger phrases suffice, proposes why separately trained LoRAs can cross-combine, and attributes lower KOALA image quality to limited model capacity. The earlier limitation concerning highly abstract styles is retained and moved into the conclusion.

D1.justification: V2 supplies more explicit trigger-phrase annotations and guidance, discloses unlabeled user comparisons with arbitrary ordering, and adds the ablation-study interface. SDXL hyperparameters, block assignments, hardware timings, and project/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds KOALA and DiT references and removes the LEGO discussion and citation. It also revises the characterization of B-LoRA's training and its contrast with UnZipLoRA. The broader literature positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: prompt construction moves into the problem setup, preliminaries and comparisons are condensed, experimental subsections are restructured, and limitations enter the conclusion. The supplement gains a contents list and reorders implementation details, experiments, and compute requirements.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is reformatted, qualitative panels are redistributed, and v1 Figures 6 and 12 are consolidated into v2 Figure 13. V2 expands Table 1, adds Tables 3–4, introduces application and sensitivity figures, and expands the user-study interface display.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the retained method: quantitative component ablations replace reliance on selected qualitative examples, while prompt and column-fraction tests address previously untested sensitivities. Separate recontextualization evaluation further supports the compatibility claim. Some interpretations remain overstated: M2 receives only 39.51% style preference over M1 despite claimed style improvement, and uncertainty estimates remain absent. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.
